title: Many Cards, Many Banks — How to Handle Them
sub: One total debt, or separate? Which to settle first? A worked example.

topic: "I have 5 cards in 4 banks — is it one big debt?"

heading: How banks actually see it
source: Each card is its own account and its own contract
items: Each card = a separate account, separate dues, separate settlement
Different banks never combine — each bank settles only its own dues
Same bank, many cards or loans: ask for ONE letter covering all of them
One default is reported to CIBIL — every lender sees it
Other banks may cut your limits or close your cards

heading: Example: 5 cards, 4 banks, ₹5.2 lakh total
note: Illustrative. Numbers are principal (what was actually spent).
tag: Not one ₹5.2L debt — four separate negotiations

heading: What to protect & settle first
note: General order — your own situation decides.
rows: Loans / EMIs with auto-debit or cheque (bounce = criminal risk)
The bank that holds your salary / savings account (set-off risk)
The bank giving the best written offer — close it fully
Next bank — one at a time, each with its own letter

items.text: Paying ₹1,000 here and there to every bank — closes nothing
Keep one sheet: bank, card's last 4 digits, principal, offer, status
Every settled card: its own letter + NOC + CIBIL check
Never use one card to settle another
